stack: Native Android (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose), MVVM + Hilt DI, Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Realtime + Storage)
stage: Pre-release / internal distribution (signed APK sideload, no Play Store)

architecture.rationale: Verified via src/ layout: clean MVVM + Hilt + type-safe Compose navigation. Data, screens, navigation, updater layers separated. RegistrationDraft shared holder added without disturbing the 9 screens. Minor: cross-screen flow state held in AppNavigation composable rather than a ViewModel (works, slightly unusual).

code_quality.rationale: Verified via read_file + grep: consistent Compose style, detekt/ktlint configured (run on-demand), ProGuard minify enabled. 3 TODOs, harmless 'Mock*' naming left as fallback (cosmantic). No swallowed exceptions in core paths; errors surfaced via SupabaseRepository.lastError.

security.rationale: Verified: RLS enabled on all 14 tables (001 has 14 ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY) + per-parent storage policies (003, private buckets). anon key only in client — grep confirms NO service_role/sb_secret in source; secrets gitignored (*.jks, keystore.properties, supabase.properties) and never committed. RISK: self-updater (AppUpdater) downloads + installs GitHub release APK with NO hash/signature verification — only a version-string compare. HTTPS alone is insufficient per self-update integrity guidance.

testing.rationale: Verified: unit tests exist (AuthRepositoryTest, SupabaseRepositoryTest, DataModelTest, MockDataTest, SupabaseConfigTest, RouteTest) and build. BUT they assert 'network layer never throws', not real auth/authorization/role-gate behaviour. No integration/E2E test of signup -> register -> invoice loop (README admits this). Critical authz paths untested by automation.

documentation.rationale: Verified: README.md is thorough (prereqs, layout, Supabase config, DB setup steps 001-003, build, release/signing, architecture notes, known limitations). Gaps: no CI docs, README slightly stale (says isMinifyEnabled=false but build.gradle sets true). supabase.properties template documented inline; no standalone .env.example.

deployment.rationale: Verified: signed release build works (v1.1.0, versionCode 2), keystore backed up off-machine (C:/Users/USER-PC/A+StudyHouse-KEYSTORE-BACKUP/), migrations tracked in repo (001-004), ProGuard on. RISKS: no CI/CD pipeline (.github/workflows absent); no automated rollback; Supabase free-tier auto-pause (~weekly) causes full outage — flagged for a keep-alive ping.

performance.rationale: Verified via read_file of SupabaseRepository/SupabaseRealtime: REST over OkHttp + direct Phoenix WebSocket (no heavy SDK dependency), no N+1 or unbounded queries in inspected data paths. No runtime profiling was performed (load/latency not measured), but the implementation shows no obvious red flags and is appropriate for an aftercare-centre app at this scale.

maintainability.rationale: Verified: single config layer (BuildConfig from gitignored supabase.properties), detekt baseline, consistent package structure, Hilt DI. Easy onboarding from README. Minor: no CI means regressions caught only manually.

important.title: Self-updater installs APK without integrity verification
important.problem: AppUpdater.downloadApk() fetches the GitHub release asset and installIntent() launches it with only a semver compare (isNewer). No SHA-256/hash or signing-certificate pin check before install.
important.impact: If the GitHub repo or release asset is compromised, a malicious APK installs silently with the app's own permissions (full data access). HTTPS does not prevent a tampered release asset.
important.evidence: Verified — AppUpdater.kt lines 116-146: downloadApk returns file, installIntent builds ACTION_INSTALL_PACKAGE; no hash/signature verification anywhere in checkForUpdate/downloadApk/installIntent.
important.action: Before install, verify a pinned SHA-256 of the downloaded APK (store the expected hash per release tag, or sign releases with a fixed cert and compare the APK signing-certificate). Reject on mismatch.

important.title: No automated tests for auth, role-gating, or the core registration->payment flow
important.problem: Existing unit tests assert the network layer never throws; they do not exercise login, RLS-enforced row access, admin vs parent role gates, or the 9-step registration -> application -> proof-of-payment persistence.
important.impact: An authz regression (e.g. a parent seeing another family's data, or a broken submit) could ship undetected. This is the highest-risk untested path.
important.evidence: Verified — app/src/test has AuthRepositoryTest/SupabaseRepositoryTest/etc.; README 'Known limitations' states no E2E/device test of signup->register->invoice loop. No test references auth.uid()/role assertions.
important.action: Add at least: (1) a Supabase auth login/logout test, (2) a role-gate test asserting a parent cannot read another parent's application row via RLS, (3) a happy-path registration submit test against a test project.

important.title: No CI/CD pipeline; Supabase free tier auto-pauses
important.problem: Builds are manual (./gradlew assembleRelease). The Supabase project is free tier, which pauses after ~1 week idle, causing every network call to fail until manually resumed.
important.impact: No automated quality gate on push; a paused DB reads as a full app outage to users (login, registration, payments all fail) until someone notices and resumes it.
important.evidence: Verified — no .github/workflows in repo; README 'Known limitations' lists no CI. Supabase free-tier pause behaviour confirmed earlier this session (521/fetch-failed until dashboard resume).
important.action: Add a GitHub Action that runs detekt + unit tests on push, and a daily keep-alive ping (simple authenticated SELECT) to stop the DB pausing; document recovery steps in README.
